picks.title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
picks.rationale: This is a new decision on the Oct 17 story. After backlash, Meta struck the Commercial Terms clause that let it crawl advertiser-linked sites for AI training, which changes what advertisers agree to before the Oct 30 effective date.
picks.excerpt: Meta struck the Commercial Terms language that suggested it could crawl websites 'associated with' business/advertiser accounts to train AI, after backlash; a spokesperson said crawling practice hasn't changed.

picks.title: ChatGPT Traffic Drop Appears To Be A Tracking Problem
picks.rationale: This is an attribution issue that matters right away. The apparent drop in ChatGPT referrals comes from links that open without tracking tags, so marketers measuring AI-driven visits and conversions are undercounting.
picks.excerpt: ChatGPT-attributed referral traffic fell sharply in several analytics datasets this month; analysts tie it to ChatGPT links opening without tracking tags, an attribution issue for marketers measuring AI-driven visits.

picks.title: VideoAmp Bets On AI To Connect Ad Planning And Measurement
picks.rationale: This is the measurement angle on agentic TV buying. Fresh off its JIC re-certification, VideoAmp is using AI agents to tie TV planning to measurement so buyers can optimize campaigns in flight.
picks.excerpt: With its JIC re-certification in hand, VideoAmp is pushing AI agents to connect TV planning and measurement so buyers can optimize campaigns in flight.

picks.title: Google Ads PM says target or budget changes cause no learning period
picks.rationale: Google's automated Smart Bidding now scales bids proportionally to new targets without resetting learning, and a re-engagement mode is reaching PMax first. Buyers can now change targets and budgets mid-flight.
picks.excerpt: Google Ads PM Tal Akabas said Smart Bidding now scales bids proportionally to new targets on steady campaigns without re-entering learning; a re-engagement mode reaches PMax first, with Search and Shopping next.

picks.title: Brands turn to content series and Jimi Hendrix to improve AI search performance
picks.rationale: Named brands, Fender and Marshall, are moving brand budget into content series and site overhauls built to feed the models behind ChatGPT and other chatbots. It is a concrete case of spend shifting toward AI-answer visibility.
picks.excerpt: Fender and Marshall are funding branded content series and site overhauls partly to give the models behind ChatGPT and other chatbots more to work with, as brands shift spend toward AI-search visibility.
